conditions: The record is a Linear issue.
The issue belongs to a team that is private.
That team's profile describes that team as owning offline sync.

turn2.differences: No material difference. Author c1-c4 cover the same requirements as Step 1: an issue belonging to a team, that team has MOB in its key, its profile says it owns offline sync, and it is private.
turn2.naturalness_note: A real user would name the team or issue directly (e.g. Mobile / MOB-1 / title). Identifying the team by privacy flag plus key substring plus profile wording, while leaving 'the issue' otherwise unidentified, reads as constructed to force a lookup.

records.note: Team t-mob: key MOB contains MOB, private true, description owns offline sync for field crews.
Team t-sup: MOB appears in name/displayName MOB Support, but key is SUP so fails key condition; private and description pass.
Team t-and: key AND does not contain MOB; private and description pass.
Team t-mobx: key MOBX contains MOB and private true, but description is prototypes/spikes, not owning offline sync.
Team t-mobp: key MOBP contains MOB and description owns offline sync, but private is false.
Team t-web: key WEB, description marketing site, public team; fails key, description and private.
